engines.title: Bragg grating
engines.description: Coupling coefficient, peak reflectance, bandwidth and exact stack reflectance of a Bragg grating.
references: H. Kogelnik, in Guided-Wave Optoelectronics, ed. T. Tamir (Springer, 1988)
M. Born and E. Wolf, Principles of Optics, §1.6 (characteristic matrices)

coupling_coefficient.title: Coupling coefficient κ
equations: κ = 2 Δn sin(π m f) / (m λ)

grating_summary.title: Peak reflectance and bandwidth
equations: Δλ_null = λ^2 / (π n_g L) sqrt((κL)^2 + π^2)

stack_reflectance.title: Quarter-wave or arbitrary periodic stack
equations: M = [[cos δ, -i sin δ / n], [-i n sin δ, cos δ]]

engines.title: Gaussian beam
engines.description: TEM00 beam radius, curvature, Gouy phase, Rayleigh range and thin-lens focusing.
references: A. E. Siegman, Lasers (University Science Books, 1986), ch. 17 and 20

engines.title: Dissipative idler channel
engines.description: Continuous and lumped idler loss in a parametric amplifier — spectral loss profiles, exact undepleted-pump gain with idler dumps and/or distributed absorption, and the adiabatic (strong-loss) limit. Used by opa_chi2 and opa_chi3.
references: R. W. Boyd, Nonlinear Optics, 3rd ed. (Academic Press, 2008), §2.9
M. E. Marhic, Fiber Optical Parametric Amplifiers, Oscillators and Related Devices (Cambridge, 2007)

linear_gain.title: Gain with idler loss
equations: d/dz [s, c] = [[-α_s/2, iΓ], [-iΓ, iΔk - α_i/2]] [s, c],  c = a_i* e^{iΔkz}
dumps at z = kL/(N+1): c → 10^(-dB/20) c
strong loss: g_s = Γ² α_i / ((α_i/2)² + Δk²)

outputs.name: idler_photon_conversion
outputs.label: Idler photons out / signal photon in

loss_spectrum.title: Loss profile
equations: pass: w = ½[tanh((λ - c + W/2)/e) - tanh((λ - c - W/2)/e)]
α_i(λ) = α_i,peak w(λ),  dump(λ) = dB_peak w(λ)

engines.title: Material refractive index
engines.description: Sellmeier phase and group index of SiO2, Si3N4, LiNbO3 (e, o), LiTaO3 (approximate) and Si.
references: I. H. Malitson, JOSA 55, 1205 (1965)
D. E. Zelmon, D. L. Small, D. Jundt, JOSA B 14, 3319 (1997)
K. Luke et al., Opt. Lett. 40, 4823 (2015)

engines.title: χ² optical parametric amplifier
engines.description: Gain coefficient, small-signal gain, full coupled-wave propagation with pump depletion, and QPM gain spectra, all with an optional dissipative idler (continuous and lumped) for ω_p = ω_s + ω_i in guided modes.
references: R. W. Boyd, Nonlinear Optics, 3rd ed. (Academic Press, 2008), §2.8–2.9
J. A. Armstrong, N. Bloembergen, J. Ducuing, P. S. Pershan, Phys. Rev. 127, 1918 (1962)
M. M. Fejer, G. A. Magel, D. H. Jundt, R. L. Byer, IEEE J. Quantum Electron. 28, 2631 (1992)

coupling.title: Gain coefficient Γ
equations: θ = ∫ e_p e_s e_i dA = (2/π)^{3/2} π / [(w_p⁻² + w_s⁻² + w_i⁻²) w_p w_s w_i]
Γ = 2 d_eff θ √(ħ ω_p ω_s ω_i F_p / (2 ε0 c³ n_p n_s n_i)),  F_p = P_p/(ħ ω_p)

small_signal_gain.title: Small-signal gain
equations: with idler loss: d/dz [s, c] = [[0, iΓ], [-iΓ, iΔk - α_i/2]] [s, c], dumps c → 10^(-dB/20) c

coupled_wave.title: Coupled-wave propagation
equations: da_p/dz = i K a_s a_i e^{-iΔkz} - α_p a_p/2
da_s/dz = i K a_p a_i* e^{iΔkz} - α_s a_s/2
da_i/dz = i K a_p a_s* e^{iΔkz} - α_i a_i/2

gain_spectrum.title: QPM gain spectrum
equations: G(λ_s) = 1 + (Γ/g)² sinh²(gL), or the idler_loss solution with α_i w(λ_i), dB w(λ_i)

engines.title: χ³ fibre parametric amplifier
engines.description: Degenerate-pump four-wave-mixing amplification 2ω_p = ω_s + ω_i with SPM/XPM — nonlinear coefficient, small-signal gain, coupled-wave propagation with depletion, Taylor and exact step-index-fibre gain spectra, all with an optional dissipative idler (continuous and lumped).
references: G. P. Agrawal, Nonlinear Fiber Optics, 5th ed. (Academic Press, 2013), ch. 10
J. Hansryd, P. A. Andrekson, M. Westlund, J. Li, P.-O. Hedekvist, IEEE J. Sel. Top. Quantum Electron. 8, 506 (2002)
M. E. Marhic, Fiber Optical Parametric Amplifiers, Oscillators and Related Devices (Cambridge, 2007)

coupling.title: Nonlinear coefficient γ
equations: A_eff = 1/∫e_p² e_s e_i dA = (π/2)² w_p² w_s w_i (2w_p⁻² + w_s⁻² + w_i⁻²)/π  (πw² for equal radii)
γ = n2 ω_p / (c A_eff),  γ_j = γ ω_j/ω_p

small_signal_gain.title: Small-signal gain
equations: G_s = 1 + (rP/g)² sinh²(gL)  (lossless); with idler loss the idler_loss solution, Γ = rP, Δk → κ

gain_spectrum.title: Gain spectrum (β2, β4)
equations: Δβ = β2 Ω² + β4 Ω⁴/12,  Ω = ω_s - ω_p
κ = Δβ + 2γP = 0 at the gain peak

fiber_gain_spectrum.title: Fibre gain spectrum (exact Δβ)
equations: Δβ(λ_s) from the LP01 n_eff at λ_s, λ_i, λ_p
γ from the four-wave Gaussian overlap at each λ_s

engines.title: Three-wave phase matching
engines.description: Phase mismatch, QPM period of any order, coherence length and sinc² response for ω3 = ω1 + ω2 with arbitrary mode indices (bulk, birefringent or modal).
references: M. M. Fejer, G. A. Magel, D. H. Jundt, R. L. Byer, IEEE J. Quantum Electron. 28, 2631 (1992)
R. W. Boyd, Nonlinear Optics, 3rd ed. (Academic Press, 2008), ch. 2

engines.title: QPM second-harmonic generation
engines.description: Phase mismatch, first-order poling period, coherence length and QPM bandwidth for SHG.
references: M. M. Fejer, G. A. Magel, D. H. Jundt, R. L. Byer, IEEE J. Quantum Electron. 28, 2631 (1992)

engines.title: Slab waveguide modes
engines.description: Effective index, V and b of a three-layer slab mode (multilayer stacks via multilayer_neff in Python).
references: K. Okamoto, Fundamentals of Optical Waveguides, 2nd ed. (Academic Press, 2006), ch. 2

slab_neff.title: Three-layer slab mode
equations: k d sqrt(n_f^2 - N^2) = m pi + atan(r_s γ_s / κ) + atan(r_c γ_c / κ)

engines.title: Step-index fibre LP01 mode
engines.description: LP01 effective index, V number and mode-field radius of a silica step-index fibre.
references: D. Gloge, Appl. Opt. 10, 2252 (1971)
D. Marcuse, Bell Syst. Tech. J. 56, 703 (1977)

lp01.title: LP01 mode
equations: U J1(U)/J0(U) = W K1(W)/K0(W), U² + W² = V²
